facility_roles.quote: DZero is one of two detectors positioned along the four-mile Tevatron accelerator ring.

facility_roles.note: The Tevatron proton-antiproton beams that D0 records are produced and accelerated entirely at Fermilab.

intervals.label: design and construction (inferred bound)
intervals.note: No source explicitly labels this whole period "construction"; it is the sourced gap between D0's 1984 approval and its 1992-05 start of data-taking. Status is an inference; both bounding dates are independently sourced.
intervals.quote: The impetus was a decision by the Fermilab Program Advisory Committee to call for a new general purpose detector whose focus ... would complement the CDF detector at B0.

intervals.label: Run I
intervals.locator: INSPIRE experiment record 1109214; corroborated by "The D0 experiment enjoyed a very successful data-collection run at the Fermilab Tevatron collider between 1992 and 1996" (Upgraded D0 Detector, NIM A565, 2006)
intervals.note: End year precision only (1996); no month given by either source.

intervals.label: shutdown for Run II upgrade
intervals.locator: Upgraded D0 Detector, NIM A565 (2006), abstract
intervals.quote: Since then, the detector has been upgraded to take advantage of improvements to the Tevatron and to enhance its physics capabilities.

intervals.label: Run II
intervals.quote: After an extensive upgrade to the muon, tracking, trigger, and data acquisition systems, the DZero experiment ran from 2001 to 2011.

intervals.label: Tevatron shutdown; D0 data-taking ends
intervals.locator: news.fnal.gov, "Tevatron shuts down, but analysis continues" (2011-09); fnal.gov Shutdown Process page; d0.fnal.gov home page
intervals.note: d0.fnal.gov confirms: "The DØ experiment finished data collection in 2011 when the Tevatron collider run ended and now is analyzing the collected data set."
intervals.quote: When the Tevatron shut down on Sept. 30, 2011, scientists first stopped the CDF and DZero detectors. ... The DZero detector was completely shut down after about three months.

quantity.note: Approximate figure ("about 5,500-ton", not a survey-precision number) as stated on the fnal.gov Tevatron Experiments: DZero page; no independent detector-paper mass figure was found to cross-check it against this session.
quantity.quote: The 5,500-ton detector sits more than four stories tall and is composed of more than 1 million individual detector elements.

physics_goals.quote: The impetus was a decision by the Fermilab Program Advisory Committee to call for a new general purpose detector whose focus (electron and muon identification, excellent calorimetric energy and spatial resolution) would complement the CDF detector at B0.
physics_goals.value: General-purpose study of proton-antiproton collisions: quantum chromodynamics, electroweak physics, and searches for new phenomena, with an initial detector focus on electron and muon identification and calorimetric precision complementary to CDF

summary.plain: A giant particle detector at Fermilab, near Chicago, named after its position on the Tevatron collider ring. It watched protons and antiprotons collide from 1992 until the Tevatron shut down in 2011, and it co-discovered the top quark in 1995.
summary.technical: General-purpose proton-antiproton collider detector at the D0 interaction hall on the Fermilab Tevatron ring, complementary in design to CDF at B0. Uranium/liquid-argon calorimetry with (post-Run I) a central tracking system and 2 T solenoid added for Run II. Co-discovered the top quark with CDF in 1995. Ran Run I (1992-1996) and Run II (2001-2011), ending with the Tevatron shutdown of 30 September 2011.
